name: Libyan Bazin
description: Bazin, a firm, dome-shaped barley dough served with a well of meat stew poured over the top, is widely considered Libya's national dish, traditionally eaten by hand from the shared dome.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour with boiling water into a very firm, smooth dough, kneading until it holds a dome shape.
Brown the lamb with the cumin, 6-7 minutes, then add the tomatoes and simmer 15-18 minutes.
Shape the dough into a dome on a serving plate and pour the stew into a well at the center.

name: Libyan Shorba Libiya
description: Shorba libiya, a spiced lamb and tomato soup with orzo-like pasta and mint, is a beloved Libyan dish, especially eaten to break the fast during Ramadan.
steps_detailed: Brown the lamb, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and 2 cups water, and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the orzo and simmer 8-10 minutes until tender.
Stir in the mint before serving.

name: Libyan Shakshuka
description: Shakshuka, eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce, shared across the wider North African region, a common Libyan breakfast.
steps_detailed: Simmer the tomatoes, bell pepper, and cumin 10-12 minutes into a thick sauce.
Make wells and crack the eggs in.
Cover and cook 5-6 minutes until the whites are set.

name: Libyan Mbatten
description: Mbatten, a layered eggplant and meat casserole with egg custard on top, a genuine Libyan specialty, similar in spirit to Greek moussaka.
steps_detailed: Salt the eggplant slices and let sit 15 minutes, then pat dry and pan-fry until golden, 6-7 minutes.
Brown the beef with the tomatoes, 8-9 minutes.
Layer the eggplant and beef in a baking dish, pour the beaten egg over the top.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 20-22 minutes until the egg is set and golden.

name: Libyan Asida
description: Asida, a smooth wheat porridge served with a well of butter and honey or date syrup, a genuine Libyan celebration dish, especially for childbirth and holidays.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour into 1.5 cups boiling water and cook, stirring constantly, 10-12 minutes until thick and smooth.
Serve with a well of melted butter and honey poured over the top.

description: Batata mubattana, potato slices sandwiched around spiced meat and fried, a beloved Libyan snack.

Fry, turning, 4-5 minutes per side, until the potato is golden and cooked through.
